bc_debeck_s_hill.blurb: A small bolted crag tucked into the forest above Alice Lake, near Squamish. Twelve sport routes run from easy 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, with most of the lines sitting in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The wall is split into two tiers: a lower band of roughly 20 m climbs beneath big trees, and a slightly taller upper band that catches morning and midday light. Expect shade and some moss in damp spells. The cliff sits right beside a wide forest track, so the mood is relaxed and the walk is short, which suits a quick half-day of mileage.
bc_debeck_s_hill.parking_note: Leave the car in the southernmost lot at Alice Lake Provincial Park, at the south end of the lake where the Jack's Trail and DeBeck's Hill trails start.
bc_debeck_s_hill.approach: From the south lot, walk to the turnaround loop and go through the gate onto the wide forest road, keeping right at the first fork. The crag appears on the left beside the road after about 15 to 20 minutes of steady uphill.

bc_stave_lake.blurb: A lakeshore climbing area on the upper shore of Stave Lake in the Fraser Valley, near Mission. Twelve lines mix boulder problems and traverses over water with a few short trad cracks, bolted slab and a top rope. Boulder grades mostly run V1 to V5, while the roped climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.11. The rock is gritty with good friction. The cliffs face east, so they warm up early and fall into shade by late afternoon, which makes the area best as a summer outing. Bring shoes you do not mind soaking and a brush.
